story: Alaska's governor race as the statewide vote on data centers, with the winner inheriting a pending land transfer and a military data-center lease offer at the noon December 7th handoff

claims.claim: With 11% of precincts reporting on election night, Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins led the first-round count for Alaska governor with 55% of the vote.
claims.verbatim: With 11% of precincts reporting, Kreiss-Tomkins leads with 55% of the vote.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Published November 3, 2026 at 8:51 PM AKST. Partial early count; say early returns. Division of Elections results pages returned 503.

claims.claim: In the same early count, Republican Bernadette Wilson was second with 28%.
claims.verbatim: Bernadette Wilson is in second with 28%
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: In the same early count, Republican Dave Bronson was third with 11%.
claims.verbatim: Dave Bronson is in third with 11%
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Do not confuse with the 11% of precincts in C01.

claims.claim: In the same early count, Republican Treg Taylor was fourth with 6%.
claims.verbatim: Treg Taylor is in fourth with 6%
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: The Anchorage Daily News reported Kreiss-Tomkins at 55.3% of first-choice votes as of 8:40 p.m., with 45 of 400 precincts reporting.
claims.verbatim: had 55.3% of first-choice votes tallied as of 8:40 p.m., with 45 of 400 precincts reporting
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News
claims.notes: Same story: Wilson 27.5%, Bronson 10.8%, Taylor 6.2%. 45 of 400 is 11.25%.

claims.claim: The Anchorage Daily News reported just over 65,000 ballots counted as of Tuesday evening.
claims.verbatim: just over 65,000 ballots counted as of Tuesday evening
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News

claims.claim: The Anchorage Daily News reported that Kreiss-Tomkins would become Alaska's first Democratic governor since 2002 if he keeps his lead.
claims.verbatim: Alaska's first Democratic governor since 2002
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News

claims.claim: If no governor candidate wins more than 50% in the first round, the race will be decided by ranked choice voting on November 18th.
claims.verbatim: If no candidate gets more than 50% in the first round, the winner will be decided by ranked choice voting on Nov. 18.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: The winner of the governor's race is set to take office at noon on December 7th.
claims.verbatim: The winner is set to take office at noon Dec. 7.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: December 7th, 2026 is the first Monday in December.

claims.claim: The Alaska Constitution sets the governor's four-year term to begin at noon on the first Monday in December after the election.
claims.value: noon on the first Monday in December
claims.verbatim: The term of office of the governor is four years, beginning at noon on the first Monday in December following his election
claims.source_outlet: Constitution of the State of Alaska, Article III, Section 4 (Wikisource transcription)

claims.claim: Election officials plan to certify the general election by November 25th.
claims.verbatim: Election officials plan to certify the election by Nov. 25.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: Based on historical trends, results reported on election night in Alaska tend to represent around 70% of the overall vote.
claims.verbatim: Based on historical trends, the results reported on Election Night tend to represent around 70% of the overall vote
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins said at a September 8th forum in Anchorage that he supports a moratorium on data center development in Alaska until the Legislature passes a regulatory framework.
claims.verbatim: I support a moratorium on data center development in Alaska until the Legislature can pass a comprehensive regulatory framework for that development in Alaska
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: By James Brooks. Background, his stated position.

claims.claim: Wilson said by text message that she would never allow Alaska to be littered with hyperscale data centers.
claims.verbatim: I will never allow Alaska to be littered with hyperscale data centers that take our resources and spoil our lands.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Hyperscale specifically; not opposition to all data centers.

claims.claim: Bronson said he is a big believer in data centers.
claims.verbatim: I'm a big believer in data centers.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: Taylor said of data centers that Alaska needs to embrace it.
claims.verbatim: "I think we need to embrace it," he said of data centers.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: Taylor said data centers can produce a net savings to Alaska ratepayers.
claims.verbatim: "It can produce a net savings to the ratepayers in Alaska," he said.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins said in Fairbanks in mid-October that he thinks Alaska should pause on data centers.
claims.verbatim: "I think we should pause," Kreiss-Tomkins said.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Next line: 'We should make sure that we have laws in place that protect the public interest.'

claims.claim: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said in Fairbanks on October 14th that people want to drop 10 billion on a data center without tax breaks.
claims.verbatim: We have people knocking on our door that want to drop 10 billion on a data center, and they don't want any tax breaks,
claims.source_outlet: KUAC via Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: The Alaska Senate voted 14 to 5 this year to pass a data center bill.
claims.verbatim: This year, the Alaska Senate voted 14-5 to pass a data center bill,
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Article link points to SB 250 on BASIS; BASIS returned 403.

claims.claim: The Alaska House did not take up the Senate-passed data center bill before the legislative session ended.
claims.value: House did not take it up
claims.verbatim: but the House failed to take it up before the end of the legislative session.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: The Pentagon has offered to lease about 4,700 acres of government land in Alaska to private companies for data centers.
claims.verbatim: It's offered to lease about 4,700 acres of government land to private companies, though no projects have been awarded yet.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC and American Homefront Project via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Page says the Pentagon; no solicitation number.

claims.claim: The Pentagon wants up to a dozen new military data centers near Anchorage, Healy and Fairbanks.
claims.verbatim: The Pentagon wants to build up to a dozen new military data centers near Anchorage, Healy and Fairbanks.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC and American Homefront Project via Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: As of September 15th, no Alaska military data center lease projects had been awarded.
claims.verbatim: though no projects have been awarded yet
claims.source_outlet: KUAC and American Homefront Project via Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: Sen. Lisa Murkowski said she is not a proponent of data centers at JBER or Alaska's Interior military installations, citing an insecure energy base.
claims.verbatim: I am not a proponent of data centers down at JBER or at our Interior installations because we are not able to support them because of an insecure energy base at this time,
claims.source_outlet: KUAC and American Homefront Project via Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: DNR Commissioner John Crowther appeared before the Senate Resources Committee under a rare legislative subpoena.
claims.verbatim: Under a rare legislative subpoena, DNR Commissioner John Crowther appeared before the Senate Resources Committee on Monday
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: Asked whether DNR could decide the 20,000-acre Mat-Su transfer before a new governor takes office December 7th, Crowther said it is certainly possible.
claims.verbatim: it's certainly possible
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: The state could transfer 20,000 acres near Houston to AIDEA for a proposed industrial and energy district that could include data center development.
claims.verbatim: The state could transfer 20,000 acres near Houston to its economic development agency
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: DNR is reviewing more than 2,100 public comments before a final decision on the Mat-Su transfer.
claims.verbatim: DNR is now reviewing more than 2,100 public comments before issuing a final decision.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: AIDEA officials have maintained that data centers are unlikely in the Mat-Su development because it lacks a reliable energy source.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA officials have maintained that it is unlikely that data centers would be part of the development in the Mat-Su
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: Another 885 acres at Port MacKenzie are slated for no-cost transfer to AIDEA.
claims.verbatim: another 885 acres at Port MacKenzie slated for transfer to AIDEA
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, republished by Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Rail-support and cargo logistics, not a data center site.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins had raised $1.8 million for his governor campaign by late July.
claims.verbatim: Kreiss-Tomkins has brought in $1.8 million since entering the race in February.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News via Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: Six Anthropic employees collectively gave Kreiss-Tomkins $372,000, making them among his top contributors.
claims.verbatim: His top contributors include six employees of Anthropic, a California-based artificial intelligence company, who collectively gave Kreiss-Tomkins $372,000.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Individual employee gifts, not company contributions. As of July.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins's largest contribution, $100,000, came from an Anthropic employee.
claims.verbatim: Thomas gave the campaign $100,000, and Kreiss-Tomkins said that Thomas connected him with other Anthropic employees
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Do not name the private individual in the deck.

claims.claim: Alaska's U.S. Senate race has drawn more money from employees of AI companies than any other 2026 Senate race, according to Stanford student journalists published by the Alaska Beacon.
claims.value: more than any other 2026 Senate race
claims.verbatim: Alaska's U.S. Senate race has drawn more money to campaigns from employees of AI companies than any other 2026 Senate race
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon
claims.notes: Verified via the Beacon RSS feed (article URL 403s).

claims.claim: At least 19 AI-company employees contributed approximately $119,000 to the campaigns of Sen. Dan Sullivan and Mary Peltola.
claims.verbatim: at least 19 employees contributed approximately $119,000 to the campaigns of Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon

claims.claim: Peltola received at least $56,000 from AI-company employees, nearly all of it from Anthropic employees.
claims.verbatim: Peltola received at least $56,000
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon
claims.notes: Continues 'nearly all of it from Anthropic employees.'

claims.claim: Sullivan received approximately $63,000 from AI-company employees for his campaign.
claims.verbatim: Sullivan received approximately $63,000 from AI-company employees for his campaign.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon

claims.claim: Another $35,000 in AI-company employee money went to Sullivan's leadership PAC, True North.
claims.verbatim: Another $35,000 came through his leadership PAC, True North.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon

claims.claim: About 150 Fairbanks residents attended a data center town hall at the Wedgewood Resort on Thursday night, October 29th.
claims.verbatim: About 150 Fairbanks community members gathered at the Wedgewood Resort Thursday night
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU/KTVF)
claims.notes: Thursday inferred as October 29th. Single source; also quotes a supporter.

claims.claim: Legislators Scott Kawasaki, Maxine Dibert, Mike Prax and David Guttenberg attended the Fairbanks town hall.
claims.verbatim: Scott Kawasaki, Maxine Dibert, Mike Prax and David Guttenberg.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU/KTVF)

claims.claim: Town hall organizer Sarah Hollister said the community's largest concern is that nobody asked them.
claims.verbatim: Our largest concern is that nobody asked us.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU/KTVF)

claims.claim: The University of Alaska Board of Regents meets November 4th through 6th on the University of Alaska Fairbanks campus.
claims.verbatim: will meet in Fairbanks, November 4-6, on the University of Alaska Fairbanks (UAF) campus
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska (news release via EIN Presswire)

claims.claim: UA Chief Information Technology Officer Ben Shier will present the latest version of UA's AI Engaged effort to the regents.
claims.verbatim: Chief Information Technology Officer Ben Shier will share the latest version of UA's "AI Engaged" effort.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska (news release via EIN Presswire)

claims.claim: UA's AI Engaged statement establishes six guiding principles.
claims.verbatim: The statement establishes six guiding principles, four investment priorities and five system-wide expectations
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska (news release via EIN Presswire)

claims.claim: UA's AI Engaged statement establishes four investment priorities.
claims.verbatim: The statement establishes six guiding principles, four investment priorities and five system-wide expectations
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska (news release via EIN Presswire)

claims.claim: UA's AI Engaged statement establishes five system-wide expectations.
claims.verbatim: The statement establishes six guiding principles, four investment priorities and five system-wide expectations
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska (news release via EIN Presswire)

claims.claim: UA says AI Engaged preserves UAA, UAF and UAS responsibility for curriculum, academic integrity and faculty instructional judgment.
claims.value: curriculum, academic integrity and faculty instructional judgment
claims.verbatim: preserving UAA, UAF and UAS responsibility for curriculum, academic integrity and faculty instructional judgment
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska (news release via EIN Presswire)

claims.claim: UAA associate professors Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter wrote in an Anchorage Daily News opinion piece that Anthropic's Claude generated the initial draft of UA's AI plan, a fact they say was concealed until October 9th.
claims.verbatim: Anthropic's Claude generated the initial draft, a fact concealed for months until Oct. 9.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion)

claims.claim: According to the same op-ed, the UA Board of Regents will vote on November 5th on the AI plan.
claims.verbatim: Now, the University of Alaska Board of Regents will vote on Nov. 5 to enshrine Claude's pro-artificial intelligence vision.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion)

killed.claim: Sen. Cathy Giessel said 'This is a violation of our legislative appropriation authority'.
killed.why: Not on the cited page; her words there differ. Scout quote garbled.

killed.claim: The Air Force data center lease is solicitation AFCEC-26-R-0006.
The lease sites are at JBER, Eielson and Clear.
killed.why: The page names Anchorage, Healy and Fairbanks; Clear is not mentioned.

killed.claim: The Air Force (enhanced use lease) is offering the 4,700 acres.
AIDEA told lawmakers data centers are unlikely in Mat-Su.
killed.why: Page says 'have maintained'; softened as C30.

killed.claim: The Crowther hearing was held October 26th.
The Senate race drew the 'most of any' race per a 'Stanford analysis'.
killed.why: Neither phrase on the page; corrected as C35.

killed.claim: SB 250 title, sponsor, vote date and House status per BASIS.
killed.why: BASIS returned 403; only the secondary 14-5 report survives.

killed.claim: A newer first-round governor count than 8:40 to 8:51 p.m.
killed.why: Division of Elections pages 503; no newer count verified.

killed.claim: Bronson added 'I know that might be unpopular with some folks here'.
Roger Kaye opinion on Kreiss-Tomkins AI planks.

killed.why: Verified but not about AI; left out.
